notes: Independent identity assessment: cover and article title identify A psychological intervention reduces doping likelihood in Italian athletes: A replication and extension; authors Kavussanu, Rubaltelli, Leo, Hurst, Giovannoni, Barkoukis, Lucidi, D’Ambrogio and Ring; DOI 10.1016/j.psychsport.2024.102761; Psychology of Sport & Exercise 77 (2025) 102761. This matches the neutral replication reference. Cover identifies Publisher’s PDF/Version of record. Supplied file is a frozen primary-report PDF parse of selected overlapping page windows, not a complete transcription. No local PDF supplied; no rendering or acquisition performed. P markers are zero-based PDF pages including cover, so P6/P7 correspond to article pp.6/7. Missing windows cannot establish absence from the full work. The two supplied descriptions identify neither outcome nor particular time/condition contrast, omnibus effect, or simple slope. Study 1 and page locators admit multiple tests. Requested metric alone cannot establish target correspondence. No target selected by row order or numeric matching. Common-model candidate N=118 athletes is explicitly printed in section 3.1 and Table 3; exclusions are two athletes under 16 and one with incomplete pre-intervention measures, with no other missing data. Screening N=540 athletes/46 clubs and recruitment N=121 are separate roles. Common N retained only in dispositions for parent field-scope review, as instructed for unresolved row correspondence. No N derived from df or group sum. Original side is an unassigned placeholder and does not assess original-paper availability. Reported success is the authors’ broad study-level narrative verdict; it does not assert that every outcome replicated identically. Tables 3 and 4 explicitly report unstandardised regression coefficients, but many outcomes, time comparisons, condition contrasts and simple slopes match p.7. Metric identity is established; target row identity is not.
